# Flossie Tulk

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019), [v1 c38 P40](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0040)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)</sub>

## Appearance

Flossie is a heavy girl, considered too heavy to believably play a fairy queen. She maintains an innate physical dexterity despite her weight.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)_

## Personality

Flossie is caustic-tongued, bold, and unpleasant, possessing a spiteful and haughty demeanor. She lacks creative imagination and struggles with arithmetic, but is never hesitant to speak up or ask questions. She is superstitious, believing that the number thirteen brings terrible luck, and frequently harbors malicious joy at the expense or humiliation of others.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P47](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0047), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c30 P31](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0031), [v1 c31 P28](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0028), [v1 c32 P7](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0007), [v1 c32 P42](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0042), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033)_

## History

Flossie attended Brierley school, where she frequently engaged in rivalries and dares, such as successfully walking along the crest of the wooden garden fence when challenged by Nell Harcourt. She took part in school activities under Miss Thorne, though she grew moody after losing the role of the fairy queen in a school dialogue due to her weight. She won the top prize for knitted lace at the Exhibition and later joined the Regent's Entrance preparation class. Although arithmetic proved to be a hurdle, she passed the Entrance examination by a narrow three-point margin. Upon moving to town to attend Regent's Academy, she took Second Class coursework, resided in the same lodging as Frank Stockley, and traveled in Hugh Carrow's carriage.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c29 P24](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0024), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c31 P28](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0028), [v1 c32 P42](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0042), [v1 c33 P34](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0034), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)_
